summary.text: 大 is a whole-graph picture of a frontal human figure and is commonly used to mean “big” or “great.” Whether the figure’s arms hang down or extend outward is disputed; “adult” as an earlier sense is proposed, not established by a dated semantic sequence.

formation.text: Pictographic: the whole graph depicts a frontal human figure. Descriptions differ on whether the arms hang down or extend outward, so the pose is unsettled; both accounts identify a human figure.

components.text: The whole graph is analyzed as a frontal standing adult human, not as a combination of smaller signs. Descriptions differ on the arms’ position; the figure and its proposed original sense remain interpretations.

history.text: Historical sources label forms as oracle-bone, bronze, small-seal and standard script, with the standard form described as close to small seal. The curated examples are modern redrawings that show broad stylistic differences, not a precise sequence of stroke changes.
An Eastern Han dictionary explanation says 大 depicts a human and records it as an ancient form of 亣. This is an early historical account of the graph, not independent proof of its prehistoric origin.

uncertainties.text: The earliest precisely dated use meaning “adult” or “big” is unresolved. A bronze inscription is cited for “big,” but its specific vessel and date are not established.

The proposed development from “adult” to “big” lacks a dated sequence of intermediate uses. The broad script labels likewise do not establish specific graphic changes, corruption or variant chronology.

senses.text: A specialist analysis proposes “adult,” contrasted with child, as an early sense; a precisely dated attestation for this use is unresolved.
A bronze inscription is cited using 大 for “big,” opposite 小; the specific vessel and date are unresolved.
大 is currently used with senses including “big,” “great,” “vast,” “large” and “high.”

developments.text: An analysis proposes that “big” developed from “adult,” but intermediate stages are not documented in a dated sequence.

limitations.text: The proposed adult-to-big development is an interpretation rather than a dated chain of attestations; the earliest precisely dated sense remains unresolved.
Modern glosses do not establish a historical sequence among “big,” “great,” “vast,” “large” and “high.”

items.period: Shang oracle-bone script style; the redraw is not a securely dated specimen.
items.caption: This modern redraw in Shang oracle-bone script style shows 大 as a frontal human figure, with a long upright body, slanting side strokes, and separated legs. Sources agree on the human-figure interpretation but differ on how to read the pose.
items.alt: Black glyph with a long upright center, two slanting side strokes, and separated legs.
items.selection_reason: This early-style form illustrates the whole-graph human-figure analysis. Its shape does not resolve the differing interpretations of the pose.

limitations.text: These redrawings represent script styles rather than photographs of ancient objects. The human-figure interpretation is shared, but accounts differ on the pose; the shapes alone cannot establish the figure’s original meaning.
